chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 463: Li Sui Goes Missing & The Skinned Dog’s Grin
chapter_meta_description: After the Heavenly Calamity, Li Huowang wakes blind and exhausted, only to discover his parasitic “daughter” Li Sui has vanished. The search leads to a chilling visitor at the window.
og_title: Something Missing — Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 463
og_description: Blind and broken, Li Huowang searches for Li Sui… but what answers his call is not his daughter.
twitter_title: Ch. 463: A blind father, a missing child, and a skinned dog at the window.
twitter_description: He calls for Li Sui. The thing that answers wears a dog’s flayed face.

lore_anchors.definition: An ontological disaster in the Dao-Twisted World that removes or corrupts a fundamental law of reality, not to be confused with a xianxia tribulation.
A high-order fate entity in the Dao-Twisted World; Li Huowang confirms that what he saw was not a Siming, implying a category of being above or outside that hierarchy.
An ancient Chinese ritual vessel used to inscribe permanent records; in the novel, the entity’s body functions the same way, recording truth without lies.
A corrupting spiritual force used by the White Lotus; Bai Lingmiao’s silence suggests she has not fully purged it.
A parasitic entity spawned by twisted cultivation; Li Sui is a fragment of it, making her disappearance an event of unknown danger.
The assistant medium in a chuma ritual; Bai Lingmiao’s Second Spirit warns Li Huowang about the false Li Sui.
A folk-horror image where a familiar entity is reduced to a hollow mimic; its vocal imitation of Li Sui inverts the protective symbolism of a dog into something predatory.
The Way of Sitting in Forgetfulness—a secret society of liars and tricksters who weaponize deception; the faceless member taunts Li Huowang as part of their psychological predation.
